title: Pigeon and Fox
paragraphs:
**Pigeon:**
By day, the city is mine.
I strut across the square in my smart grey suit
while buses grumble up the high street
and people spill out of the station
like marbles from a bag.
Every café table is my breakfast.

**Fox:**
By night, the city is mine.
When the last bus has rumbled home to bed,
I slip out of my den by the railway line
and glide through the shadows like smoke.
The moon is my streetlamp,
and every dustbin is a feast.

**Pigeon:**
Your city? You leave it in a terrible mess!
You knock the lids off the bins,
drag chicken bones across the pavement
and leave muddy pawprints on the cars.
And who has to tidy up the crumbs? Me!

**Fox:**
And what about you, featherbrain?
You squabble over one soggy chip,
you flap in people’s faces,
and you sit on the statue’s head all day
as if you owned the place.

**Pigeon:**
Hmph. But when you trot home at dawn,
tired and muddy,
I still leave you the crust of my breakfast
on the station wall.

**Fox:**
I know. And when I pass your windowsill at night,
I tread softly
so that I don’t wake you.

**Pigeon and Fox:**
By day,
by night,
the city is ours.

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 1.
Find and copy **one** word that shows Pigeon walks in a proud, showy way.

Look at verse 1.
People spill out of the station ‘like marbles from a bag’.
What does this suggest? Tick **one**.
options: The people are carrying bags of marbles.
Lots of people rush out of the station at once, going in all directions.
Only a few people leave the station, one at a time.
The people are playing a game outside the station.

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 2.
Fox says that he glides ‘through the shadows like smoke’.
What does this tell you about the way Fox moves?
questions.model: Fox moves smoothly and silently, and he is hard to see in the dark, just like smoke drifting through the shadows.
points: explaining that Fox moves smoothly, quietly or secretly, or that he is hard to see.

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 2.
‘When the last bus has rumbled home to bed’
What does this tell you about when Fox comes out? Tick **one**.
options: early in the morning, when the first buses start
at lunchtime, when the cafés are busy
late at night, after the buses have stopped
after school, when the buses are full

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 4.
‘You squabble over one soggy chip’
Which word is closest in meaning to **squabble**? Tick **one**.
options: share
argue
dance
sing

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 4.
Fox calls Pigeon ‘featherbrain’.
What does this suggest? Tick **one**.
options: Fox thinks Pigeon is clever.
Fox thinks Pigeon is silly.
Fox is frightened of Pigeon.
Fox wants to borrow Pigeon’s feathers.

questions.prompt:
Look at verse 5.
Where does Pigeon leave the crust for Fox?
accept: on the wall of the station
on the wall at the station
on the wall by the station

questions.prompt:
Look at the whole poem.
Tick **one** box in each row to show whether each statement is **true** or **false**.
statements: Pigeon says that Fox leaves muddy pawprints on the cars.
Pigeon walks across the square at night.
Fox says that Pigeon flaps in people’s faces.
Fox passes Pigeon’s windowsill in the daytime.

questions.prompt: How is the poem organised? Tick **one**.
options: Pigeon speaks in the first half of the poem, and Fox speaks in the second half.
A narrator describes Pigeon and Fox, but they never speak.
Each verse describes the city at a different time of year.
Pigeon and Fox take turns to speak, and in the last verse they speak together.

questions.prompt: Using the whole poem, give **two** ways that Pigeon’s life in the city is different from Fox’s.
questions.model: Pigeon is out in the city by day, but Fox only comes out at night, after the last bus. Also, Pigeon eats from café tables, but Fox finds his food in dustbins.
points: each difference that makes clear what is different for the two animals (1 mark each), such as:
Pigeon is out by day, but Fox comes out by night
Pigeon eats from café tables, but Fox eats from dustbins
Pigeon struts across the square, but Fox slips and glides through the shadows
Fox lives in a den by the railway line, but Pigeon has a windowsill
Fox is messy (he knocks the lids off the bins), but Pigeon tidies up the crumbs

questions.prompt:
Look at verses 3 to 6.
How do Pigeon and Fox really feel about each other?
Explain, using evidence from the poem.
questions.model: On the surface, they seem to dislike each other and they argue: Pigeon says Fox leaves the city ‘in a terrible mess’, and Fox calls Pigeon ‘featherbrain’. But really they care about each other: Pigeon still leaves Fox ‘the crust of my breakfast’, and Fox treads softly past Pigeon’s windowsill ‘so that I don’t wake you’.
points: Explains that they seem to dislike each other or argue, with evidence, such as ‘You leave it in a terrible mess!’ or ‘featherbrain’.
Explains that really they care about each other, with evidence, such as Pigeon leaving ‘the crust of my breakfast’ or Fox treading softly ‘so that I don’t wake you’.

questions.prompt:
What do you think will happen the next time Pigeon and Fox meet?
Use evidence from the poem to support your prediction.
questions.model: I think they will argue and call each other names again, because they enjoy complaining about each other: Fox calls Pigeon ‘featherbrain’. But I think they will still look after each other, because Pigeon leaves Fox ‘the crust of my breakfast’ and Fox treads softly ‘so that I don’t wake you’.
points: a sensible prediction (1 mark), e.g. they will argue again but still be kind to each other; they will share the city; Pigeon will leave Fox some food.

evidence from the poem that supports the prediction (1 mark), e.g. they argue (‘featherbrain’; ‘You leave it in a terrible mess!’); Pigeon still leaves Fox ‘the crust of my breakfast’; Fox treads softly past Pigeon’s windowsill; at the end they say ‘the city is ours’.

questions.prompt: Which is the best summary of the whole poem? Tick **one**.
options: A fox chases a pigeon through the city streets at night.
A pigeon and a fox leave the busy city to live in the countryside.
A pigeon and a fox argue about who owns the city, but they secretly care about each other and share it.
A pigeon teaches a fox how to find food in the daytime.
